avoid_supplements.name: Oral Iron Supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Concurrent use increases risk of iron overload and toxicity; ferric carboxymaltose is already providing IV iron
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue all oral iron supplements during and for at least 5 days after IV ferric carboxymaltose administration

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin C (>2000 mg/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increases iron absorption and oxidative stress; may potentiate iron-induced tissue damage
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin C supplementation to <1000 mg/day; avoid megadoses during iron treatment

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May reduce oral iron absorption if taken concurrently, though minimal impact with IV administration
caution_supplements.action: Space administration by 2+ hours if patient also takes oral iron; monitor iron levels

caution_supplements.name: Polyphenol-rich supplements (Green tea extract, Resveratrol)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May chelate iron and reduce bioavailability of future oral iron therapy
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum ferritin and iron levels; no dose adjustment typically needed

avoid_foods.name: High-dose iron-fortified cereals and supplements combined
avoid_foods.mechanism: Risk of iron overload when combined with IV ferric carboxymaltose
avoid_foods.action: Counsel patients to avoid deliberate iron fortification intake during treatment period

caution_foods.name: Tea and Coffee (high tannin content)
caution_foods.mechanism: Tannins chelate iron and reduce oral iron absorption; minimal impact on IV iron but relevant if transitioning to oral therapy
caution_foods.action: No strict avoidance needed but limit consumption near any future oral iron doses

caution_foods.name: Calcium-rich dairy products
caution_foods.mechanism: May interfere with oral iron absorption in patients transitioning from IV therapy
caution_foods.action: Space dairy intake from oral iron supplements by 2+ hours if applicable

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods (whole grains, legumes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Phytates and fiber may reduce oral iron bioavailability; not relevant to IV administration
caution_foods.action: Relevant only for future oral iron supplementation; maintain normal dietary fiber intake

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hemoglobin/hematocrit regularly during and after treatment. Assess for signs of iron overload (abdominal pain, joint pain, cardiac arrhythmias) and ensure discontinuation of all oral iron products for minimum 5 days post-infusion.
